text: Survey responses from blockchain using private investment fund advisers show that their fee structure deviates from the traditional 2/20 model, with responding managers reporting alternative fee structures that benefited their clients.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Applications and Fee Structure Developments in Private Investment Funds (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2959730

isBasedOn.name: Blockchain Applications and Fee Structure Developments in Private Investment Funds

abstract: The graph illustrates that the fee structure of those private investment fund advisers that use blockchain technology (and responded to the survey) deviates from the traditional 2/20 model.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: n=59 survey responses drawn from the dataset
the author could not obtain responses from all managers in the dataset
